title: Add release-manifest-checksum and migration-sweep operator for downgrade safety
author: Ana Rodrigues
description: Motivation: Upgrades followed by emergency downgrades have exposed gaps where minor manifest drift or opaque schema changes cause partial restores and data divergence. This PR introduces two coordinated safety primitives: (1) a release-manifest checksum recorded at every installer release and persisted to the cluster as an immutable ReleaseLock CRD, and (2) a migration-sweep operator which validates post-upgrade migration side-effects and produces an automated remediation plan before allowing rollback. Summary of changes: adds ReleaseLock CRD and controller, a lightweight migration-sweep operator, helm hooks to create pre-upgrade snapshot and post-upgrade checksum, terraform provider change to write release lock to state when running installer, installer CLI "redwoodctl installer verify-lock" command, and e2e test harness updates. Checklist: - [x] Add ReleaseLock CRD and controller with RBAC rules - [x] Implement helm hook templates (pre-upgrade snapshot, post-upgrade checksum) - [x] Add migration-sweep operator and plan-generator - [x] Expose CLI command to query/validate release locks - [x] Integrate terraform plan guard to block apply when manifest drift detected - [x] Add e2e tests (backup/restore with simulated downgrade) - [x] Add docs section and runbook entries Design notes: The ReleaseLock CRD stores the helm release manifest checksum (SHA256) plus an operator-generated manifest fingerprint and a list of migration-tokens (semver+migration-hash). The installer writes a ReleaseLock during successful apply and marks it immutable; subsequent releases create new ReleaseLock objects. The migration-sweep operator runs post-upgrade to perform a set of read-only probes (schema checks, vector index sanity, KV namespace validation) and stores a MigrationSweepReport as an annotation on the current ReleaseLock. If any probe fails, the operator will populate a remediation plan and, depending on policy, either block the automatic rollback or mark the rollback as advisory. Usage: - Installer (helm/terraform) will emit a pre-upgrade etcd snapshot via helm pre-hook and then run post-upgrade checksum hook; the controller verifies checksum matches expected. - redwoodctl installer verify-lock --cluster <id> will return the active lock and migration report. - TF provider includes a plan-time check: if the remote ReleaseLock checksum does not match local release artifact, the apply is paused and plan shows a descriptive message. Safety guarantees: - Prevents silent downgrades where schema/migration state mismatches exist. - Provides an auditable manifest fingerprint linked to backups and terraform state. Rollback flow: - If a downgrade is requested, migration-sweep operator runs in dry-run to surface regressions. - If reports are clean, rollback proceeds. If not, operator writes remediation steps and requires explicit --force-downgrade to continue. Testing: unit tests for controller reconciliation, integration tests simulating a failed migration (index missing), and e2e scenario that performs upgrade -> migration failure -> attempted rollback and verifies behavior. Ops/runbook: added a new runbook page (docs/ops/downgrade-safety.md) describing how to interpret MigrationSweepReport, how to force a rollback, and recommended remediation steps. Backwards compatibility: ReleaseLock objects are created only after this release; installer will not block older clusters but will surface a warning when rollback is potentially unsafe. Implementation notes: schema migration checks are pluggable; default probes include Postgres schema checksum, Redis namespace keyspace check, and Milvus/vector-search index sanity. Future work: add optional automated rollback pausing with human-in-the-loop approval flow and OPA policy gating.
commits: feat(crd): add ReleaseLock CRD and controller with immutable lock semantics
feat(operator): migration-sweep operator with probe runner and plan generator
chore(helm): add pre-upgrade snapshot and post-upgrade checksum hooks
feat(tf): add plan-time release-lock validation to provider
cli: add redwoodctl installer verify-lock command
review_comments: Jamal Patel: Nice approach. Two questions: (1) How do we ensure ReleaseLock itself can't be tampered with in hosted/private scenarios? (reply) Ana: ReleaseLock is written with ownerReferences and a webhook admission policy; for private installs we additionally recommend enabling KMS-backed sealed-secrets for the release artifacts, doc updated.

Priya Nambiar: Can the migration-sweep be expensive? We need SLO for probe time. (reply) Ana: Default probe set is bounded and runs with a 30s per-probe timeout; operator exposes metrics and we added a config to limit concurrency.

Ethan Liu: TF provider blocking apply is risky for existing automation. Suggest opt-in flag. (reply) Ana: Added provider flag 'release_lock_enforce' default=false; terraform plan will now include a warning unless the flag is enabled in module.
ci_summary: CI: unit tests passed; integration suite ran with the new e2e scenario. Flake in unrelated SDK test (flaky network), rerun succeeded. All checks green: lint, unit, integration, e2e (partial).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge after approvals from Jamal and Priya. No merge conflicts. Changelog entry added under docs/CHANGELOG.md.
release_notes: Adds ReleaseLock CRD and migration-sweep operator to prevent unsafe downgrades. Installer now emits pre-upgrade snapshots and post-upgrade checksums. New CLI and Terraform opt-in guard to validate release manifests at plan/apply time. Operational runbook included.
notes_for_backport: Backport to the 1.3.x maintenance branch requires bundling the CRD YAML and the migration-sweep operator image tag; test plan included in backport checklist.
